topics.title: Domestic Violence & Car Bomb Investigation
topics.summary: Police responded to a domestic violence call at the Hogan home in West Babylon where he was charged with misdemeanor assault. Separately, authorities investigated a former teacher’s alleged use of a homemade bomb to damage a car linked to his firing from a Catholic school, fueled by rumors and targeting.

topics.title: Bushwick Explains a Near-Fatal Attempt
topics.summary: During an interview, Bushwick Bill recounts his desperate attempt to obtain insurance money by staging his own suicide after being provoked into shooting him with a rifle. He describes the chaotic aftermath – including a panicked escape and subsequent survival of surgery – highlighting the bizarre circumstances surrounding the event.

topics.title: Bullet in the Eye Rap Battle - Contract Dispute
topics.summary: A rapper demands $20 million for a gunshot wound to the eye, disputing a $5000 contract offered by record labels. He claims it’s insufficient compensation for ten years of hardship and then bizarrely accuses record companies of hiring thugs to attack him before demanding an absurd sum.

topics.title: Clinton, Scandals & Czech Presidents
topics.summary: The broadcast discusses the ongoing investigation into President Clinton’s relationship with Monica Lewinsky, including potential release of taped testimony from the grand jury. Calls for impeachment continue alongside discussions about congressional debates and an unusual encounter between Clinton and Czechoslovakian president Havel who requested Lou Reed play him songs.”

topics.title: Lewinsky Scandal Discussion
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, hosts discuss the Lewinsky scandal and its implications for President Clinton’s future, referencing public opinion regarding impeachment versus resignation while engaging in light banter about personal frustrations.

topics.title: Repetitive ‘Oh, My Balls Are Rattling’ Segment
topics.summary: The program features a prolonged segment where the host repeatedly states "Oh, my balls are rattling." Later segments include commentary on television ratings and talk shows, followed by discussion about President Clinton's forgiveness and an anecdote regarding actress Mia Farrow selling Spice Girl memorabilia for charity.
